headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist via shared API/MCP-style integration; prompt-injection and capability-conflict are lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dexter can write to .dexter/scratchpad/ and operates autonomously, while MemMachine exposes an MCP Server. That creates a plausible content-bridging path where attacker-controlled text from one agent can be reinterpreted by the other. The interaction is not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Dexter writes untrusted text into .dexter/scratchpad/ and MemMachine reads it through MCP or API glue, injection is possible.
IF the orchestrator forwards one agent's raw outputs into the other's prompt without sanitization, prompt hijacking becomes feasible.
mitigations: Add a strict content separator and instruction/data tagging in the bridge.
Disable automatic ingestion of scratchpad files into prompts.
Require allowlisted schemas for MCP payloads.
Manually review any cross-agent text before reuse.
requires-engineering: add provenance tracking for all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple third-party APIs; MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context and also exposes an MCP Server. If either side forwards shared context or files, sensitive data can leave the pair without user awareness. The exact leakage path is not documented, so I choose high over medium due to blast radius and uncertainty.
conditions: IF Dexter sends market or financial data to external APIs, those contents may be exposed outside the local workspace.
IF MemMachine receives user history through MCP or API calls, long-term preferences and conversational context can be retained or relayed.
mitigations: Restrict Dexter API keys to non-sensitive test data.
Block MemMachine from receiving raw financial files or prompts.
Use separate principals and workspaces for each agent.
Turn off any automatic logging or transcript export.
requires-engineering: enforce field-level redaction before cross-agent transfer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dexter supports multiple instances and writes to .dexter/scratchpad/, while MemMachine is reachable through REST, SDK, or MCP. Overlap exists on mutable integration surfaces, but the profiles do not show both agents writing the same directory or shared git state. That makes conflict plausible in default orchestration, but not clearly high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same scratchpad or shared mutable workspace, writes can collide.
IF the orchestrator maps both agents to the same OAuth-backed resource, last-writer-wins conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Serialize writes through one coordinator.
Disable concurrent runs during shared-resource updates.
Use per-agent credentials and scopes.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dexter is autonomous and can emit outputs based on external APIs; MemMachine can consume those outputs through REST, SDK, or MCP. If MemMachine treats Dexter's text as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream user-facing memory or actions. The profiles do not prove direct action-taking, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF MemMachine ingests Dexter outputs without verification, hallucinations can be persisted as user facts.
IF Dexter's API-derived claims are reused as planning inputs, downstream recommendations can be wrong at scale.
mitigations: Require a verification step before MemMachine stores Dexter outputs.
Mark Dexter outputs as untrusted by default.
Add source citations to any transferred facts.
Limit automatic writeback into memory.
requires-engineering: implement confidence-based gating for downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter handles financial data and market data, while MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context. The profiles do not specify residency or retention controls, so a mismatch is plausible but not proven. Because compliance gaps can affect the same data classes across both agents, medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF financial data is routed into MemMachine's long-term memory, retention obligations may change.
IF either agent logs prompts or outputs beyond the intended retention window, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Avoid storing financial data in long-term memory.
Review retention settings for both agents.
Separate regulated and non-regulated workflows.
Document data-flow boundaries.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement.
